canonicalControl.universe: registered EQUITY_UNIVERSE with the canonical Dow PIT membership schedule

unit.primary: rank-priority canonical replacement pair at a rebalance
unit.pairing: sort removals by current canonical rank and additions by current canonical rank, then pair in order; pairing is bookkeeping because canonical logic has no security-to-security identity
unit.window: current rebalance open through next rebalance open for both securities
unit.censoring: last-rebalance pairs without a subsequent rebalance and pairs lacking either security's executable prices are excluded; unmatched additions/removals caused by canonical cash-slot changes are reported, not fabricated

outcomes.primary: incoming next-period return minus outgoing counterfactual next-period return

rank: outgoing rank deterioration = current minus prior rank
recentPath: 20-session acceleration = recent 20-session return minus one-third of 60-session return
outgoingState: close MFE and MAE to decision
features.prohibited: No additional feature library, classifier, machine-learning model, or post-result threshold search

buckets.continuousDiagnostics: sample quartiles, fixed before outcomes are summarized; quartiles are descriptive and not candidate rules
buckets.winnerNearMfe: profitable and capture of close MFE to decision at least 75%
buckets.winnerHighGiveback: profitable and current unrealized return captures less than 50% of close MFE
buckets.loserMaterialRecovery: currently non-positive and recovery from close MAE is at least max(1 percentage point, 25% of absolute MAE)
buckets.loserNearMae: currently non-positive and recovery from close MAE is less than 1 percentage point

archetypes.strongUpgrade: rank gap at least 6 and outgoing rank deterioration at least 6
archetypes.hotEntrant: incoming 20-session return in the top sample quartile
archetypes.decayingIncumbent: outgoing MFE giveback in the top sample quartile
archetypes.loserRemoval: outgoing currently non-positive and outgoing 20-session return negative

statistics.goodVsBad: means, medians, standardized mean differences, and cluster-bootstrap mean-difference intervals; no classifier
statistics.nullCalibration: 2000 cluster-structure-preserving outcome shuffles, seed 20260822; compare the strongest absolute observed Spearman correlation across the predeclared continuous features with the shuffled maximum
statistics.multipleTestingInterpretation: descriptive; the max-relationship null check guards against promoting the strongest of several variables by chance

economicMagnitude.eventContribution: equal-slot arithmetic: sum replacement advantage divided by canonical top-N
economicMagnitude.annualization: equal-slot arithmetic contribution divided by the five-year development span
economicMagnitude.groupShare: group equal-slot contribution divided by total canonical replacement contribution, with sign instability disclosed

badReplacementConcentration: worst five pairs, worst 1/3/5 rebalance-cluster shares of total negative event shortfall, and leave-one-cluster-out mean range

drawdownPeriods.additionalRequested: For 2024 and 2026, use the largest equity peak-to-trough episode whose trough occurs in that calendar year; if none exists, report no episode. No regime rule will be inferred.

mrmComparison: Use the same event construction and compact rank/score diagnostics on canonical Market-Residual Momentum; score magnitudes are strategy-specific and will not be compared directly across formulas.
decisionRule: Recommend exactly one future preregistered modification concept only if an interpretable relationship is economically material, spans multiple independent clusters, is not dominated by a few events, and the max-relationship null calibration is directionally supportive. Otherwise conclude that no narrow replacement modification is currently justified.
